label: code-comment-carries-no-lasting-fact
name: A code comment cites review rounds, tracker ids or the feature that added it, or a Note narrates a fix instead of an invariant
description: What breaks: a reader in two years learns nothing technical. 'PR 4596 review round 4, comment W3' in a production header and in a test (4146947611 'probably don't want to reference ... like this', 4146959502 'Scrub please'); 'Story 2814' in Note [GOF staging eviction] (3350285744 'don't mention Story numbers in comments'); a three-line comment tying a general-purpose TRACE_EVENT to the feature Note (3350412400 'It's a useful event no matter the context'); a 13-line Note [Fixed KV-head slot geometry] for a plain stride bug fix (3866668853 'not worthy of it's own noisy Note'). Procedure: grep added comment lines for PR #, review, round, comment W<n>/R<n>-M<n>, Story, ticket, JIRA, reviewer names; flag added Note blocks whose content narrates a fix rather than an invariant other code will cite; flag comments that attribute a general statement to the PR's feature. Check 9 applies the same reader test to the PR body; this applies it to code comments and Notes. Contrast with workaround-needs-tracking: a TODO beside temporary behavior is wanted, a tracker id in an explanatory comment is not.
disposition_reason: Check 9 runs only inside Status/Verification sections of the PR body; the reader test must also run on added comment lines and new Note blocks.
agent_feasibility: yes: regex over added comment lines plus a length/content test for new Note blocks.

members.concern: A code comment in the production header cites the PR review round and reviewer comment label ('PR 4596 review round 4, ...'); such review-history references do not belong in code.

detection.trigger: An added comment line in any source or test file contains a PR number plus 'review', 'round', 'comment W<n>' / 'R<n>-M<n>', or a reviewer's name as the reason for the code.
detection.procedure: `git diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^\+.*(review round|round [0-9]|comment W[0-9]|R[0-9]-M[0-9]|PR [0-9]+ review)'` over h/, src/ and t/. For each hit, rewrite the comment to state the lasting technical reason (what the code guarantees and why), dropping the review provenance. Count the hits so the ask says 'there are more'.
detection.question: Does the comment explain the code by citing who asked for it in a review instead of the lasting reason the code is this way?

detection.procedure: Same grep over t/; after the first hit keep going and report the count, so the ask covers every instance ('seems there are more').
detection.question: Does the comment explain the test by citing the review that asked for it rather than the behavior it pins?

members.concern: A code comment (the new Note [GOF staging eviction]) cites a work-tracker item ('Story 2814'); he asks to drop the tracker reference from code comments and offers the reworded line as a suggestion block.

detection.trigger: An added or changed code comment (not the PR body) contains a work-tracker or review reference: 'Story N', 'ticket', 'JIRA', 'issue #', 'PR #', 'review round', 'as discussed with'.
detection.procedure: grep the added lines of the diff for 'Story', 'Ticket', 'JIRA', 'PR #', 'issue #', 'round' inside comment lines (// or /* ... */). For each hit, rewrite the sentence without the reference and check that the technical content still stands on its own.
detection.question: Would a reader of this comment in two years, with no access to the tracker, lose any technical fact if the reference were removed?

Author reply 2026-06-09: removed.

members.concern: Wade objects to adding a long named Note (Note [Fixed KV-head slot geometry], a 13-line comment block) for what is a plain bug fix in the K transfer stride, since a Note is for an algorithm or a non-obvious strategy, not for a basic geometry correction.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a new 'Note [name]' block, or a comment longer than about 6 lines, whose content restates a fix rather than describing an algorithm, invariant or strategy that other code will cite.
detection.procedure: List every added 'Note [' title in the diff. For each, grep h/ src/ t/ at the head for 'See Note [name]' citations outside the defining file; count the lines; classify the content: algorithm/invariant/strategy versus narrative of a bug and its fix. Compare with the PR body: if the Note text repeats the body's 'Why' paragraph, it is history, not a code contract.
detection.question: Does this Note describe a mechanism future code must honor, or does it narrate the bug that this PR fixes?

members.quote: I'm not sure this (basically) bug-fix is worthy of it's own noisy Note like this. It's not like we are defining some fancy algorithm we need to document, or obtuse strategy to 'align the stars just right' ;).

members.concern: A three-line comment above a Perfetto TRACE_EVENT (a tracing span) explains it as part of the staging-eviction feature and cites the feature Note; he says the comment is unnecessary and the trace span is a general-purpose event not tied to that Note.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a comment that attributes a general-purpose statement (a trace span, a log line, a counter, an assert) to the PR's feature by name or by 'See Note [feature]', while the statement itself would be equally valid without the feature.
detection.procedure: For each added comment that cites a Note or the PR's feature, read the statement it documents. Ask whether the statement's content names anything feature-specific (an identifier introduced by the PR). If the statement is a TRACE_EVENT, spdlog call, TRON_ASSERT or counter with a generic label (here 'gof_rodeo' with 'layer'), the comment's feature link is a justification of why the author added it, not a description of what it does. Propose deleting the comment or reducing it to what the statement does.
detection.question: If the feature were reverted, would this statement stay and still make sense, and would the comment then be wrong?

codex_bullets.bullet: Identify who owns each buffer, reference, queue entry, and completion signal from submission through completion, cancellation, and reuse. Check container reallocation and scheduler storage rebuilds while references remain live.
codex_bullets.reason: Four Wade comments across PRs 2499, 2906, 4128 trace buffer and reference lifetime under DMA or reallocation; the Claude skill has no check on asynchronous ownership.

codex_bullets.bullet: Keep comments about lasting behavior and rationale. Remove review-round labels, story narration, stale questions, and debug residue. A large explanatory Note is useful only when the mechanism needs it.
codex_bullets.reason: Largest cluster in the corpus: at least 14 comments on debug residue, commented-out code, left-enabled debug macros, stale comments and review narration (also 4146959502, 2771711406, 2737935271, 2789808472, 2759903853, 3350412400, 3973917755, 3102601258, 2915191812). The positron-code-review skill covers narration but the Wade skill has nothing.
